title: Tejas: India's Light Combat Aircraft

endcard.line: Pictures: Rajan Manickavasagam (CC BY 2.0); Rahuldevnath (CC BY 3.0)

segments.say: The idea came in the late nineteen-eighties. The first flight came in two thousand and one. This is Tejas, India's Light Combat Aircraft.
It was named Tejas in two thousand and three, and joined its first Air Force squadron in July twenty sixteen. A second squadron followed in twenty twenty.
It was designed by the Aeronautical Development Agency, under DRDO, with Hindustan Aeronautics as the main partner.
Tejas is a multi-role fighter. Its shape is deliberately unstable, a trade that makes it quick and agile in the air.
Its first squadron, the Flying Daggers, had last flown the MiG-21. A home-designed jet took the place of an imported one.

anim.title: Since then
items: 2023: first exercise abroad, in the UAE

segments.say: In twenty twenty-three it flew its first exercise abroad, in the United Arab Emirates, and an order for eighty-three of the newer Mark One A is being delivered.
For GS Three, Tejas is the textbook case of indigenisation in aerospace, and of how long that road can be.

sources: PIB (relid 146717): Tejas designed by ADA (DRDO) with HAL as principal partner; first flight of TD1 on 4 January 2001; project from the late 1980s
PIB (relid 146697): Tejas inducted into No. 45 Squadron 'Flying Daggers' on 1 July 2016; the squadron last flew the MiG-21 Bis

PIB, 30 June 2023 (PRID 1936373): named Tejas in 2003; multi-role; inherently unstable design for manoeuvrability; No. 18 Squadron the second (May 2020); Ex-Desert Flag in the UAE in March 2023 was its first exercise abroad; order for 83 LCA Mk-1A
